# ADR-054 — Header-only mail storage; email is the first attacker-authored input to reach the AI layer

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Header-only mail storage, and email is the first attacker-authored input to reach the AI layer.** `mail_messages` stores identifiers, `internal_date`, sender address/domain/display name, subject, label ids, `has_attachment` and a size estimate — **and nothing else**. No body, no snippet, no payload part, no attachment content, ever, on disk or in a prompt. Every provider-supplied string carries an explicit `.max()` in Zod **and** is truncated at write, so the unbounded-`z.string()` gap recorded against `health_sessions.session_type` is not recreated. **Retention: `mail_messages` and `mail_sync_runs` are operational metadata and a bounded prune is permitted and required.** This is the first prune job in the repository and it does not conflict with ADR-047, whose no-automatic-deletion rule governs *health measurements*; the prune window must be explicit, configurable, and recorded in `docs/STATUS.md`. `mail_digests` keeps exactly one row per `(digest_date, timezone)` by upsert with no history, mirroring `ai_daily_briefs`. **ADR-024 still forbids a backup system**, so pruned mail is unrecoverable and the window must be chosen with that in mind. On the AI boundary: `MailDigestInput` is a **closed scalar allowlist** carrying no ids, no uuids, no addresses, no URLs and no bodies, with exactly **two attacker-controlled fields** — `subject` and `from_display_name` — both hard-capped. The `<snapshot>` fence holds unchanged, because `JSON.stringify` escaping is lexical and content-independent, and role separation is preserved. Three things do change, and are stated rather than assumed: the "structurally inexpressible" property now guarantees only that *our* secrets are inexpressible, not that an attacker can express nothing; the system prompt's claim that the data contains no credentials or tokens **becomes false** — subject lines routinely carry one-time codes and magic links — and must be rewritten rather than left standing as a false premise; and an attacker can inflate their own section, so the **mail section is capped hardest, capped before measurement, and is the first rung on the drop ladder**, or a third party could evict the user's own agenda from their own digest. The realistic exploit is **content laundering** — attacker text paraphrased into first-party prose that is persisted and rendered — and the defence is capability reduction plus a server-side output constraint that strips link-shaped content from persisted digest text. **No bespoke substring sanitizer is added**, per `prompt.ts`'s existing and correct reasoning that one "would give false assurance without closing anything". The guarantee is that the digest lane has **no tools**, can write nothing but text, and reaches no other table: a fully successful injection produces misleading prose, never an action. No email subject, address or display name may appear in a push body, a log line, a commit message or any status document (Phase 7 Checkpoint 7.0, user-approved 2026-08-30) **[Present state corrected by ADR-057.]**
